BarkernotBob/BarkernotBob.github.io.body:
### Which part of the site?

Publishing / deploy

### What do you want changed, and why?

Clicking Publish takes about 2 minutes to reach the live site, and most of that wait isn't the site itself. Timing from deploy run 231 (2026-09-29):

| Step | Time |
|---|---|
| `npx quartz plugin install`: re-downloads all 46 plugins from scratch, every run | **69s** |
| Setup (checkout, Node, `npm ci`) | ~18s |
| `npx quartz build`: the actual site | **9s** |
| Upload + deploy | ~20s |

Removing "fluff" won't help: `content/` is 49 files (372 KB) and builds in 9s. The fix is to cache `.quartz/plugins` in `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, keyed on `quartz.lock.json`, and skip `plugin install` when the cache hits.

### Done when...

- [ ] A deploy run with no change to `quartz.lock.json` shows the plugin install skipped (or under 10s) in the Actions log
- [ ] That run finishes in about 75s or less, end to end (it's ~2 min today)
- [ ] Changing `quartz.lock.json` makes the next run download the plugins fresh. Prove it with one run where the cache misses.
- [ ] On the live site after a cached deploy: the home page's file-tree drawer still opens on click; searching for the middle of a word still finds it; the sidebar order is unchanged
- [ ] The "~5–6 min" deploy time in `CLAUDE.md` is corrected to the measured figure

### Size

Quick - a small tweak

### Anything else?

**What it must not break.** The three plugin patches in `deploy.yml` (search `tokenize:"full"`, explorer `800px`→`99999px`, and `node patch-plugins.mjs`) must still be applied on every run, whether the cache hits or misses. The explorer patch is load-bearing for the home page (see `CLAUDE.md` → Site architecture notes).

**Build notes.**
- Save the cache **right after** `plugin install` and **before** the patches. Use `actions/cache/restore` and `actions/cache/save` as separate steps, not the all-in-one `actions/cache`, which saves at job end, after patching. That way the cached copy is always unpatched and the patches always run against a clean copy. Otherwise `patch-plugins.mjs` has to be proven safe to run twice.
- Cache key: `${{ runner.os }}-quartz-plugins-${{ hashFiles('quartz.lock.json') }}`.
- Local Preview/Publish scripts are unaffected. They don't reinstall plugins each time.
- Out of scope: app test jobs (they run in parallel with the build and don't set the total time) and trimming content.

### Original idea

> **What you asked for**
>
> Find a way to improve build speed by maybe removing fluff from the site
>
> _Filed from Dev Inbox.md (Obsidian vault), 2026-09-23._

The workflow never commits it. `pool-tool/automation/pool-reminders.yml` (and its copy at `pool-data/.github/workflows/pool-reminders.yml`) does only:

```
git add db/feed-state.json
```

So the file is written into the runner's checkout and thrown away when the job ends. `db/weather.json` does not exist in `pool-data`. The history has never accumulated past a single run.

Second, smaller problem in the same step: the commit is gated on `steps.gen.outputs.state_changed`, which is only true when a **new feed event** appeared. Even once `weather.json` is added to the `git add`, a day with new weather but no new reminder would still not commit.

This is why the app can only ever show the 30 days Open-Meteo will hand back live, and why nothing can correlate a reading against the weather from before that window.

**Done when...**

- [ ] The workflow commits `db/weather.json` as well as `db/feed-state.json`
- [ ] The commit step runs when **either** the feed state or the weather log changed, not only the former
- [ ] Both copies of the workflow are updated — `pool-tool/automation/pool-reminders.yml` is the source, `pool-data/.github/workflows/pool-reminders.yml` is the copy that actually runs
- [ ] After two consecutive nightly runs, `pool-data/db/weather.json` exists and has grown
- [ ] The app's AI export uses the stored weather history where it goes back further than the live Open-Meteo window

The fix has to change the workflow file that actually runs, `pool-data/.github/workflows/pool-reminders.yml`. The unattended nightly pass is never allowed to edit GitHub Actions workflow files.

The change is small. In the commit step:

BarkernotBob/BarkernotBob.github.io.body:
**Area:** Pool tool · **Size:** Big

**What's wrong**

Pool Care is the last app still writing one file at a time through the GitHub **Contents API**. Grocery already moved to the **Git Data API** (`quartz/static/grocery/app.js:102-105, 250, 284`) and the shared test mock already models it faithfully, including the ref-race replay. Two real defects follow from Pool being left behind.

**1. The stale-sha retry clobbers concurrent edits.** `saveJson()` (`quartz/static/pool/index.html:307`) catches a 409/422, re-reads the file for a *fresh sha*, then re-`PUT`s **its own stale in-memory array**. The other writer's change is gone.

Reproduced: a second device appends a swim entry to `log.json`; this device then marks a task done and GitHub rejects its stale sha once, as it really would. Final `log.json` contained this device's new entry and had **lost the second device's entry entirely**. No error, no warning.

`tests/pool/sync.spec.js:52` is named *"a write sends the previous sha, so a concurrent edit cannot be clobbered"* but only asserts that a sha was sent. The clobber it claims to rule out is exactly what happens. The name needs correcting along with the behaviour.

**2. Multi-file writes are not atomic.** `markTask()` commits `config.json` and then `log.json` as two separate commits. If the second fails you get a task marked done with no log entry, and nothing detects the divergence. `saveTest()` has the same shape (`tests.json`, then `config.json`).

Both are structural, and the Git Data API fixes both at once: batched blobs → tree on `base_tree` → commit → `PATCH` ref, with the deltas replayed onto fresh content on a ref race (×3) instead of overwriting.

**Done when...**

- [ ] Pool reads through ref → commit → tree → blob and writes through batched commits, matching `grocery/app.js`
- [ ] Marking a task done writes `config.json` and `log.json` in **one** commit — either both land or neither does
- [ ] A concurrent commit from a second device causes a replay onto the fresh content, not an overwrite; the second device's entry survives
- [ ] `tests/pool/sync.spec.js` uses the mock's `armRaceInject` to prove the surviving entry, and the misleading test name is corrected to say what it actually asserts
- [ ] The 1 MB Contents API ceiling no longer applies (`log.json` grows forever and has no pruning)

**Note:** #134 (double-tap and failed-retry duplication) is *not* fixed by this — that one is app logic, not transport. Both are needed.

Every save becomes a delta applied to *fresh* content: log/swim/tests are `append`, config edits are `mutate` functions that change only the fields that save touches.

**Area:** Pool tool · **Size:** Normal

**What's wrong**

Two separate bugs with the same symptom. Together they account for **11 of the 33 entries** in `pool-data/db/log.json` being duplicates: pump ×3 on 2026-09-09 within 1.2 seconds, robot ×2 on 09-03, test ×2 on 07-23 and 08-29, phosphate ×2 on 08-29, chlorine ×2 on 06-27.

**1. State is mutated before the save succeeds.** `saveTest()` does `D.tests.push(rec)` *before* calling `saveJson` (`quartz/static/pool/index.html:1249`). If the save throws, the record stays in the in-memory array. Tapping Save again pushes a *second* copy and commits both. Same pattern in `markTask()` and `logSwim()`.

Reproduced: a single 500 on the first `PUT` to `db/tests.json`, toast shows `Save failed 500: boom`, one more tap on Save, and `tests.json` ends up with two records with different ids and identical contents.

This is almost certainly the "error messages when uploading data" — the error and the duplicate are the same event.

**2. No in-flight guard on the buttons.** Two taps inside one network round trip queue two writes. Reproduced with a 700 ms delay on the GitHub `PUT` (a realistic phone round trip): two clicks on "Mark done" for one task produced two identical log entries, no error, toast said `Logged ✓`.

**Done when...**

- [x] `saveTest`, `markTask`, `logSwim` and `logChecklistDone` build the record, save it, and only add it to the in-memory array once the save has come back OK
- [x] A failed save leaves the app exactly as it was, so tapping Save again writes one record, not two
- [x] Every button that writes is disabled for the duration of its write and shows it is working — including "Done" on Today and "Mark done" on Schedule, which currently show nothing
- [x] Marking a task already logged today asks for confirmation instead of silently logging it again

BarkernotBob/BarkernotBob.github.io.body:
**Area:** Pool tool · **Size:** Quick · **Priority: do this first — it is safety-relevant.**

**What's wrong**

`saveTargets()` (`quartz/static/pool/index.html:1573`) does `parseFloat(i.value)` with no guard. Clear a box in Settings → Target ranges and save: `parseFloat('')` → `NaN` → `JSON.stringify` writes `null` into `db/config.json`.

Reproduced in a browser against the test mock. After blanking the free-chlorine "low" box, `config.targets.fc` became `{"range":[null,3]}`. Logging a free chlorine of **0.1 ppm** — a shock-now reading — then produced:

> Free chlorine (0.1 ppm): **Above 3 ppm — skip chlorine and pull the tabs** until it falls back into NaN–3 ppm.

The comparison `0.1 < null` is false, so the app falls through to the "too high" branch and tells you to stop adding chlorine when the pool has almost none.

Two related holes in the same form, worth closing at the same time:

- Nothing checks that low < high.
- Nothing checks free chlorine against total chlorine. The live `db/config.json` currently has `fc: [3,5]` and `tc: [1,3]`. Free chlorine is a subset of total chlorine, so that pair is chemically impossible — FC 4 / TC 2 would both read "in range".

**Done when...**

- [ ] A blank or non-numeric target box is rejected on save with a message saying which reading, and nothing is written to `config.json`
- [ ] A low value greater than or equal to the high value is rejected the same way
- [ ] Saving a free-chlorine range whose top exceeds the total-chlorine range's top is rejected, or the two are reconciled, with an explanation of why
- [ ] `targetRange()` falls back to the built-in range for any stored value that isn't a finite number, so an already-corrupted config self-heals on load rather than giving inverted advice
- [ ] The existing `fc: [3,5]` / `tc: [1,3]` pair in `pool-data/db/config.json` is corrected
- [ ] `tests/pool/chemistry.spec.js` covers it: a blank target saved, then a 0.1 ppm free chlorine reading, asserts the advice says shock and never says "skip chlorine"

Live `tc` range corrected from `[1,3]` to `[3,5]` to stop conflicting with `fc: [3,5]`.

**This is not buildable work** — hence `hold`. The refusals come from the session's own auto-mode permission classifier, which isn't something a change in this repo can fix. It's here so a gap in coverage is visible by name instead of vanishing into a count. A later pass must not pick it up and try to build a fix.

**Runs append a comment here rather than filing a new issue**, so a bad week doesn't produce seven copies of the same thing.

---

## 2026-08-30 — reached 15/18

Could not reach, after one retry each:

- `command-center`
- `KnoxLox`
- `feeds`

All three were refused twice, so under the protocol they're out of reach for the night rather than retryable. No open issues were missed as a result *that I can tell* — but that's precisely the point: I can't tell, because I never looked inside them.

Notable, and consistent with what #124 recorded: refusals are **not** per-repo. `obsidian-home-launch` and `obsidian-settings-pane` were both refused in a batch and both succeeded on an individual retry. `logos-notes`, unreachable on 29 Aug, was reachable tonight on the first attempt.

The refusals clustered in the one block where six `add_repo` calls went out together — 4 succeeded, 2 refused. Attaching one or two at a time went through nearly every time. Serializing plus retry-once took this run from a likely 11/18 to 15/18, which is why both are now in the protocol.

comments.body:
## 2026-08-30 (later) — gap closed, and the mechanism that caused it replaced

**All three repos are now confirmed empty.** `command-center`, `KnoxLox` and `feeds` were attached on a retry in an attended session and listed directly: zero open issues each. Nothing was missed last night — but that was luck, not the system working, which is the point of this issue.

All 18 repos in `repos.txt` are now accounted for: **5 open issues, all in this repo, and nothing anywhere else.**

### What changed

The refusals only ever mattered because the run was attaching all 18 repos every night to ask each one whether it had work. One search answers that without attaching anything, so #128 changes the scan to **search first, attach only what has issues** — typically two `add_repo` calls a night instead of eighteen. Far fewer calls, far fewer chances to be refused.

Verified before adopting: with all 18 attached, the search agrees exactly with per-repo enumeration.

### The part that is still unknown

**It has never been observed whether the search reaches a repo the session has _not_ attached** — no issue exists in an unattached repo to test with. `command-center`, `KnoxLox` and `feeds` all returned nothing both before and after attaching, which is consistent either way and therefore proves nothing.

If the search turns out to be scoped to attached repos, a repo with real work would silently never be seen. So rather than assume, every run now **audits two repos the search called empty**, rotating through sorted `repos.txt` by day-of-year. If the audit ever catches the search missing an issue, the run says so and falls back to attaching everything.

That is the honest status: the fast path is unproven at its edge, and there is now a cheap check that would catch it failing within days rather than never.

### This issue stays open

It stays on `hold` as the standing record. Runs append here when coverage is incomplete. Nothing to do — if the audit ever fires, that will show up as a comment on this issue and in the morning notification.

BarkernotBob/BarkernotBob.github.io.body:
Filed by the nightly backlog pass on 2026-08-29, about the machinery rather than a feature.

## What do you want changed, and why?

`backlog/repos.txt` lists 18 repos, and the nightly routine is supposed to scan all of them for open issues. Last night it could only reach **11**.

A cloud session starts scoped to the one repo it was launched with, and pulls the others in by calling `add_repo` per repo. Last night 7 of those calls were refused — not by GitHub, but by the session's own auto-mode permission classifier:

> Permission for this action was denied by the Claude Code auto mode classifier.

Refusals were **intermittent, not per-repo**: identical calls succeeded for some repos and failed for others in the same batch, and one repo that failed on the first attempt succeeded on a retry. So it looks like rate-limiting or a flaky classifier rather than a policy about specific repositories.

Not reached last night: 7 repos, including at least one (`logos-notes`) that the 28 Aug pass *did* reach. So the set moves between runs.

**Why it matters:** the backlog's founding rule is that an open issue is a planned item and nothing has to be tagged to qualify. A repo that silently drops out of the scan breaks that guarantee just as thoroughly as the label problem the system was built to avoid — an issue filed from a phone into an unreachable repo is invisible, and nothing in the run says so. Last night the queue happened to be in the site repo, so nothing was missed; that was luck.

## Done when...

- A nightly run either scans every repo in `repos.txt`, or reports by name which ones it could not reach
- The run's summary distinguishes "no open issues" from "could not look"
- Retrying a refused `add_repo` at least once is built in, since retries demonstrably succeed
- `backlog/README.md` documents the limitation and whatever the workaround turns out to be

## Size

Quick — most of the value is in reporting the gap rather than hiding it. Making the scan genuinely complete may be bigger and may not be fully in our control.

## Anything else?

Worth checking whether the session can be **launched** with all 18 repos as sources instead of attaching them one at a time. The Routine that fires this pass already names its sources, and the 28 Aug run shows all 18 attached, so this may be a matter of the seeded source list rather than runtime `add_repo` calls — which would sidestep the classifier entirely.

Related but separate: `.claude/commands/backlog-nightly.md` says "Only repos listed there are in scope", and that is still honoured — nothing outside `repos.txt` was touched. This is about the reverse failure, repos in scope that were never looked at.

comments.body:
Nightly pass — picking this up. Sized Quick, so it goes ahead of #112 (Big).

Useful accident: **this run reproduced the bug while building the queue**, so the numbers below are fresh evidence rather than a re-read of last night's.

## What tonight's run measured

Reached **15 of 18**. Refused: `command-center`, `KnoxLox`, `feeds` — same classifier message, and again *not* per-repo:

- `obsidian-home-launch` and `obsidian-settings-pane` were both refused in a batch, then **both succeeded on an individual retry**. That is the second night running that a retry has worked.
- The refusals clustered in the batch where I issued **six `add_repo` calls in one block** (4 succeeded, 2 refused). Attaching one or two at a time went through almost every time.
- `logos-notes` — unreachable last night — was reachable tonight on the first try. The set really does move between runs.

So the two levers that demonstrably work are **serialize** and **retry once**. Neither makes coverage guaranteed, which is why the reporting half matters more.

## On the "launch with all 18 sources" idea

Checked, and it doesn't work: `create_session` takes `source_url` — **singular, one string**. There is no seeded multi-repo source list to fix. A worker can be born holding exactly one repo and must `add_repo` its way to the other 17 at runtime, through the classifier. Ruling that out is worth recording, since it was the most promising-sounding escape hatch.

## Plan

1. `.claude/commands/backlog-nightly.md` grows a coverage protocol in step 1 — attach one repo at a time, retry a refusal once, and keep a per-repo ledger with three outcomes: **read**, **read and empty**, **could not look**.
2. Step 4's report distinguishes those three. The notification stays counts-only ("15 of 18 read") because it must not carry private repo names; the **names** go where they're durable — a comment on a standing coverage issue, reused if one is already open so a bad week doesn't file seven issues. Labelled `hold`, because a platform limitation is not build work and a future pass must not pick it up and try.
3. `backlog/routines/nightly-backlog.md` gets the retry rule added to its existing skip-and-note line. Deliberately *not* a second copy of the protocol — that file already names the command file as the authority, and two copies of this drifting apart is its own bug.
4. `backlog/README.md` documents the limitation and the workaround.
5. A regression test pinning the contract, so the retry rule and the three-state reporting can't be quietly dropped.

Files: `.claude/commands/backlog-nightly.md`, `backlog/routines/nightly-backlog.md`, `backlog/README.md`, `backlog/backlog.test.mts`. No workflow files, no `.github/` permissions.

| Done when… | How |
| --- | --- |
| Scan every repo, or report by name which it couldn't reach | Three-state ledger; names go on a reused issue |
| Summary tells "no open issues" from "could not look" | `empty` vs `unreachable`, and they may never be collapsed |

Two things worth knowing beyond the checklist:

**The "launch with all 18 sources" idea is dead.** `create_session` takes `source_url` — singular, one string. There is no seeded source list to fix, so runtime `add_repo` is the only route in and the classifier is unavoidable. That was the most promising-sounding fix in your "Anything else?", and it costs a whole run to re-derive, so it's now written down in `backlog/README.md`.

**Serializing helps more than I expected.** Tonight's refusals clustered almost entirely in the one block where I fired six `add_repo` calls at once — 4 through, 2 refused. Attaching one or two at a time went through nearly every time. Combined with retry-once, that took this run from a likely 11/18 to **15/18**.

## The counts this fix is about

Tonight: reached **15 of 18**. Unreachable after a retry each: `command-center`, `KnoxLox`, `feeds`. Under the new protocol those names would go on a `Nightly pass could not reach every repo` issue — I have not filed it tonight, because the run that would have consumed it is this one, and filing an issue to tell you about a gap I'm describing here in more detail would just be noise. From the next run on, it files itself.

## On the tests

`/code-review medium` earned its keep. One of the eight guards was **passing vacuously** — the serialization check `/one .{0,10}at a time/i` was matching "One item at a time, start to finish" from step 2, which is about issues, not repos. Deleting the real rule left the suite green. It's anchored on `repo` now, and I re-ran the mutation to prove it fails.

The review also caught that "repos read" contradicted my own ledger: `read` means "found work", so a night where all 18 attached and 12 were quiet would have reported `6/18` and looked like twelve blind spots. It now reports repos **reached** (`read` + `empty`).

Every rule is mutation-tested — six deliberate regressions, six caught. These live in prose because a model executes them, which makes them exactly as easy to delete by accident as any other paragraph, and the failure they prevent is silent by construction.

## One loose end

The branch `claude/backlog-coverage-124` is **still on the remote** — deleting it failed twice through this session's git proxy (`send-pack: unexpected disconnect`). It's fully merged into `main`, so the monthly branch sweep will clear it safely on 1 Sep; no action needed from you.

## Manual test (for Isaiah)

1. Open https://github.com/BarkernotBob/BarkernotBob.github.io/blob/main/backlog/README.md and scroll to **"Repo coverage"**. It should explain why repos go missing and why launching with all 18 attached can't work.
2. Tomorrow morning, read the push notification from the nightly run. It should end with a fraction like `15/18 repos reached` — **on every run, including a perfect one**.
3. If that number isn't `18/18`, open this repo's issues and look for **"Nightly pass could not reach every repo"**. It names which repos were missed, on which night. It's labelled `hold`, so it stays visible without a later pass trying to build it.
4. **The thing to watch for:** a run that says "nothing to do" with no coverage fraction. That's the old failure — it means the run can't tell you what it never looked at.

From the 2026-07-12 audit (`AUDIT-GAPS.md`, GAP-W7). Priority **P3**.

## What do you want changed, and why?

`.github/workflows/ci.yaml` is inherited from the upstream Quartz project and is gated on `github.repository == 'jackyzha0/quartz'`. It has therefore **never run once** in this repo. `.prettierignore` doesn't cover the apps either. So nothing has ever checked the formatting of any app code.

It shows, inside grocery itself: `domain.js`, `components.js` and `today.js` are clean, but `app.js` and `review.js` have statements crammed onto single lines — one line in `app.js` is 593 characters — and the receipt view builds its HTML out of a stack of nested one-line conditionals that nobody will be able to read in six months.

## Done when...

- A CI job checks formatting and lint across `quartz/static/{grocery,pool,vehicle,bank-bonus,shared}`
- Badly formatted app code fails the check
- The existing code is formatted once, in its own commit
- The receipt view's nested conditionals are pulled out into named helpers
- No behavior changes anywhere — the grocery suite passes before and after

## Size

Normal

## Anything else?

BarkernotBob/BarkernotBob.github.io.body:
From the 2026-07-12 audit (`AUDIT-GAPS.md`, GAP-W3). Priority **P1**, and the single biggest security finding.

## What do you want changed, and why?

When you sign in to the grocery or pool app, the request it sends asks for `scope=repo` — full read and write access to **every** private repository you own. Each app only ever needs its one data repo. If that permission ever leaked, it would hand over everything, not one grocery list.

Two ways to fix it; pick one and write down why:

- **(a)** Move to a GitHub App installed on just the data repo. Least access, more moving parts.
- **(b)** Keep the current sign-in, but make the recommended setup path a fine-grained token restricted to the one data repo, with the broad option demoted to a fallback.

Either way the Cloudflare worker docs under `pool-tool/worker/` need updating to match.

## Done when...

- The recommended setup grants access to only the relevant data repo
- `SETUP.md` / `SETUP-CHECKLIST.md` have plain-English steps for the new path
- Anyone already signed in still works — no forced re-setup
- The decision and the reason for it are written down in the repo

## Size

Normal

## Anything else?

The audit is clear that the Cloudflare worker itself is well built — the secret stays server-side, the origin is locked down, nothing is stored. Don't rewrite it. The problem is only the breadth of what's being asked for.

comments.body:
Done — merged in #121. Went with **option (b)**; the reasoning is written down in `DECISION-github-access-scope.md` (linked from `AUDIT-GAPS.md` and the Worker README), as this issue asked.

## The thing worth knowing

I could not simply narrow `scope=repo`, and it's worth saying why so nobody tries later. The "Sign in with GitHub" button is an **old-style GitHub OAuth App**, and that kind has only two settings for repositories: *public ones* (useless — your data repos are private) and *all of them*. There is no "just this one" option. Narrowing it isn't a smaller version of option (a) — it **is** option (a), which means a new app registration, rewiring the Cloudflare Worker, and everyone having to set up again. This issue ruled that last part out.

So the code still sends `scope=repo` for that button. What changed is that the apps no longer push you toward it, and now tell you what it's asking for **before** you tap it.

## What you'll see

The grocery and pool setup screens now ask for your data repo and a token up front, with a **Connect** button, and say on screen to give that token access to only that one repository. The one-tap sign-in has moved into a folded-away **"Other way in"** section that states it asks for every private repo you own.

The setup guides follow the same order, and each ends with a plain-English *"why the key, and not the one-tap button?"* — including how to take back the broad access you've already granted.

**Nothing about your current sign-in changed.** You are not being asked to redo anything, on any device, by either route. That was the acceptance criterion most at risk when I moved those fields around, so it now has a test of its own.

## Also worth knowing

The setup screen had **no test coverage at all** — every other grocery test starts already signed in, which is exactly why moving those fields was the risky part. `tests/grocery/setup.spec.js` now covers it (4 tests), including that an already-connected device is never bounced back to setup.

---

## Manual test (for Isaiah)

Roughly ten minutes, and step 1 is the important one.

**1. You are still signed in (do this first)**
1. On your phone, open `https://barkernotbob.github.io/static/grocery/`.
2. It should open **straight into your data** — no sign-in screen. Same for `.../static/pool/`.
3. If either one asks you to set up again, something's wrong: reopen this issue and say which app.

**2. Look at what a new device would now see**
1. Open a **private/incognito** browser window (Safari: tap the tabs button → **Private** → new tab).
2. Go to `https://barkernotbob.github.io/static/grocery/`.
3. You should see the setup card asking for **Private data repository** and **Access key**, with a dark **Connect** button — and a small grey line telling you to make the key so it can reach *only* your `grocery-data` repo.
4. Below that is a folded row: **▸ Other way in: Sign in with GitHub**. Tap it open. It should explain that this route asks for access to **every** private repository you own.
5. Close the private window without connecting.
6. Do the same for `https://barkernotbob.github.io/static/pool/`.

**3. Optional — move yourself onto the safer key**
Only if you want to; nothing breaks if you skip it.
1. Open https://github.com/settings/tokens?type=beta → **Generate new token**.
2. Name it `grocery app`, pick the longest expiry, choose **Only select repositories** → pick **`grocery-data`**.
3. Under **Repository permissions**, set **Contents** to **Read and write**. Generate, and copy the token.
4. In the grocery app: **Settings** → disconnect → then enter `BarkernotBob/grocery-data` and paste the token → **Connect**.
5. Once both apps are on their own tokens, you can withdraw the old wide access: https://github.com/settings/applications → find the app → **Revoke**.

**4. Read the reasoning if you like**
`DECISION-github-access-scope.md` in the repo root explains the choice, and what moving to a GitHub App would involve if you ever want the stricter option.

If any step misbehaves, reopen this issue and say which number.

From the 2026-07-12 audit (`AUDIT-GAPS.md`, GAP-W4). Priority **P2**. **This has got worse since the audit** — bank-bonus went from 78 inline handlers to 86.

## What do you want changed, and why?

All the apps live on the same web address, `barkernotbob.github.io`. That means anything running on one page can read the saved GitHub tokens belonging to the others — `gt_token`, `pl_token` and `bb_token` all sit in plain text where any script on that address can reach them.

Grocery is hardened against this: no behavior written inline in the HTML, all clicks handled in one place, and everything that shows text you typed or data pulled from GitHub goes through an escaper that neutralises it. A test enforces it.

The other three are not. Bank-bonus has 86 pieces of inline behavior, pool 39, vehicle 1. A malicious value in the weakest app can read the strongest app's token.

## Done when...

- Searching the four apps for inline `on*=` handlers returns zero results
- Each app has a test asserting that, plus one asserting a hostile value renders as harmless text
- Everything that displays typed or fetched data goes through the shared escaper (see GAP-W5)
- Each app still works when clicked through by hand

## Size

Big

## Anything else?

Order matters: **do GAP-W2 first.** This is a large mechanical rewrite of how every button works, and doing it without tests to catch a mistake is exactly the situation the audit warns about. GAP-W5 should land alongside it so the escaper being adopted is the shared one.

Nightly pass — not working this issue (it's Big and correctly ordered after #109), but the new bank-bonus suite **confirmed one of these injections is live**, so here is a concrete repro to build against.

## Confirmed working injection

Person names are rendered straight into inline handlers — `index.html` around lines **978** (`setPersonFilter`), **1613** (`setReportPerson`) and **1731** (`removePerson`):

```js
`<button class="chip" onclick="setPersonFilter('${tab}','${esc(p)}')">…</button>`
```

`esc()` (line 392) escapes `& < > "` but **not `'`**. So a person name of:

```
x'),window.__pwned=1,('
```

produces the attribute:

```
setPersonFilter('active','x'),window.__pwned=1,('')
```

— a valid comma expression. Clicking the chip runs the payload. Verified in a browser: `window.__pwned` is set. Not theoretical.

## The trap worth avoiding

**Escaping `'` as `'` does not fix this.** An event-handler attribute is HTML-decoded *before* its contents are parsed as JavaScript, so the entity turns straight back into a quote and the breakout still works. I checked this before deciding not to patch it.

That means there is no escaping-only fix for the inline-handler sites — which is exactly this issue's thesis. The structural change (no `on*=` in the HTML, one delegated click handler) is the fix, not a better escaper. Whatever `escape` GAP-W5 (#111) extracts should be documented as **for text/attribute contexts only**, never as making an inline handler safe.

## What's already in place for you

`tests/bank-bonus/security.spec.js` (merged in #119) covers the markup-injection class four ways — seeded into accounts, offers and config, plus a round trip through the Add Account dialog — and all four pass, so that class is genuinely inert today.

The handler-breakout case above is in the same file marked **`test.fail()`**, deliberately, with the repro in a comment. It is not skipped: the suite is green while the hole is open, and **the run turns red the moment you fix it** ("expected to fail but passed"). That red is your signal to delete the `test.fail()` marker — so this issue has a built-in completion check.

I deliberately did **not** patch the three sites I found by grep. This app has 86 inline handlers; a partial fix would have turned the security spec green across the 83 I haven't audited, which is worse than an honest failure.

1. Do pool and vehicle's suites first (rest of #109) — this issue already says GAP-W2 comes first, and the same reasoning applies per-app: you want the net under you before the rewrite.
2. Then the delegated-handler rewrite here, per app, watching that `test.fail()` flip.

| --- | --- | --- |
| bank-bonus | 86 | **0** |
| pool | 39 | **0** |
| grocery | 0 | 0 |
| vehicle | 1 (constant) | 1 |

Values travel in `data-*` now, where `esc()` genuinely works, and action names resolve through a fixed table rather than off `window`. I took the advice from the 29 Aug comment and did each app **wholesale** rather than sink-by-sink — with 86 sites, sink-by-sink would not have converged.

Bank-bonus needed more than pool: five event types (`blur` on the capturing phase, since it doesn't bubble), `this` becoming the element, `event.stopPropagation()`/`return false` becoming `data-stop`/`data-prevent`, and `onclick="${backFn}"` — which interpolated an entire call — becoming an action *name*.

**One thing that would have been a silent bug:** `calNav` args had to be coerced with `Number()`. `shiftMonth` does `m += delta`, so a string would concatenate — `"7" + "1"` is `"71"`, not `8` — and the calendar would have jumped to a nonexistent month. Same for `deleteDD` and `removePaycheckAmount`. Verified visually that paging goes August → September 2026.

I aligned the click attribute to grocery's existing `data-action` convention, so three of four apps now read the same way and #111 has less to reconcile.

Both of my previous comments on this issue claimed the run would turn red the moment the hole closed. **That was wrong, in both apps**, and I'd rather correct it here than leave it as folklore.

The first assertion required the payload to **land in an `onclick` attribute**. Once the attributes were gone, `idx` came back `-1`, so the test still failed — for a completely new reason — and `test.fail()` went on reporting green. I confirmed it before rewriting: with the fix in and the marker removed, it failed with `the payload should have landed in an onclick attribute — Received: -1`.

The suite was green before the fix and green after it. The "built-in completion check per app" did not exist.

Both are rewritten to assert the safety property directly: no inline handler exists, the hostile value still renders a **working** control, and clicking it executes nothing. That middle assertion matters — without it a "fix" that simply deleted the button would pass.

## Two live injections the rewrite does *not* address

`/code-review` caught these, and they're worth separating out because "we removed the handlers" would otherwise read as "this app is hardened". Both inject **markup** rather than breaking out of code, so the handler rewrite does nothing for them:

- **`promoteOffer()`** rendered person names unescaped into a `data-mval` attribute *and* a button label. The chooser only exists while its modal is open, so the existing person-name test — which walks the tabs — never reached it. Now escaped, with a test that opens the modal; I verified that test fails against the unescaped original.
- **pool's edit-task modal** wrote `value="${t.last||''}"` with no `esc()`.

The lesson from the 29 Aug comment holds and generalises: *escaping is the right fix in an attribute and the wrong fix in a handler.* These two were attributes, so escaping was exactly right.

## ⚠️ Neither suite runs in CI

The only Playwright job in `deploy.yml` is gated to `tests/grocery`. **All three checks on #126 came back `skipped`** — the green tick said nothing about this change. That's #110 (GAP-W2b), on `hold`, and workflow files are outside what the nightly pass may touch.

So the guards I added don't gate anything yet. **Until #110 lands, a future commit re-adding `onclick=` to either app ships green.** That makes #110 considerably more valuable than its `hold` label suggests.

Because CI was vacuous, the verification was local and deliberately heavier than usual:

- pool **53/53**, bank-bonus **38/38**, three runs each — stable.
- **Order-preserving cross-check** of every original call site against its new wiring: bank-bonus 86 → 83 wired + 3 bare `stopPropagation` (reconciles exactly); pool 39 → 39. All 53 action names resolve, no orphans.
- **Mutation-tested** every new guard: `onclick="…"`, `onclick='…'` and unquoted all caught. The first version of that guard only matched `on*="` and would have let single-quoted handlers straight back in; review caught it.
- **Visual confirmation** of tab nav, person filter, calendar paging, and pool's Done button.

## Why this stays open

- ❌ **"zero results across the four apps"** — vehicle still has one, `onclick="return false"` on the CarEdge bookmarklet link. A constant that interpolates nothing, and its suite pins the count at 1. The 29 Aug pass concluded with full context that vehicle doesn't need this issue, so I didn't override that unattended for something cosmetic. **One-line change if you want the literal zero.**
- ❌ **"everything goes through the shared escaper (see GAP-W5)"** — #111 shipped `quartz/static/shared/`, but pool and bank-bonus still use their own inline `esc()`. They *couldn't* migrate before, because ES modules were impossible while behaviour lived in inline handlers — which #111's own commit message says. **That blocker is now gone**, so migrating these two onto the shared layer is real, newly-unblocked work.
- ✅ Each app has a test asserting no inline handlers, plus hostile-value cover.
- ✅ Each app still works when clicked through.

My suggestion: the honest remaining scope here is "migrate pool and bank-bonus onto `quartz/static/shared/`", which is arguably #111's tail rather than this issue's. Worth deciding which issue owns it rather than having both half-claim it.

## Manual test (for Isaiah)

Both apps are live now.

1. Open **Bank Bonus Tracker** and click every tab along the bottom — Today, Active, Planned, Offers, Calendar, Reports, Settings.
2. On **Active**, tap a person's name chip (e.g. "Sam"); the list should narrow. Tap "Everyone" to undo.
3. On **Calendar**, tap `›` then `‹`. It should move forward one month and back — **not** jump to a strange year. This is the one that would break most visibly if I got it wrong.
4. On **Offers**, tap "Move to Planned" and pick a person; it should create the account as before.

**The shared escaper.** pool, bank-bonus and vehicle each carried their own `esc()` escaping `& < > "` but **not** the single quote. All three now import `quartz/static/shared/text.js`, which does. That meant making each app's script a module — possible only because #126 removed the inline handlers first: a module's top-level names aren't globals, so an `onclick="markTask(…)"` in the markup could never have resolved them. #111's own commit said this was the sequencing, and it held. - **bank-bonus rendered every tab blank.** `show()` resolved renderers with ``window[`render_${tab}`]``. Module top-level functions aren't `window` properties, so the lookup was `undefined` for all eight tabs — the app booted, drew its nav, and showed nothing. Now a fixed `RENDERERS` table, matching the `ACTIONS` convention #126 already put in that file. The same pattern was in `setPersonFilter()`.
- **None of them would have launched offline.** Each service worker precaches its shell, and `index.html` now imports a file outside it. `shared/text.js` joins each `SHELL` list, cache versions bumped.
- **The ACTIONS test would have passed vacuously.** It read `ACTIONS` off the page global — module-scoped now, so every name would have come back `undefined` and the check would have reported green over any typo. It reads the table out of the source instead.

`/code-review` flagged it and I reproduced it before touching anything: **`CacheStorage` is origin-wide.** All four apps share `barkernotbob.github.io`, so each worker's `keys.filter(k => k !== CACHE)` deleted the other three apps' precached shells on every activation. Opening bank-bonus, pool, vehicle and grocery in turn left exactly one cache each time:

```
after bank-bonus: [ 'bb-v6' ]
after pool:       [ 'poolcare-v2' ]
after vehicle:    [ 'dl-shell-v2' ]
after grocery:    [ 'gt-shell-v5' ]
```

**Only the app you opened most recently could launch offline.** That has been true for a while — it predates this branch — and it silently defeats the precache entry above. Each worker now deletes only its own name prefix; after the fix all four coexist and a cold offline start of the first app works.

Grocery's `sw.js` is touched for this and nothing else. Fixing three of four would have fixed nothing: grocery would still have evicted the rest. Same reasoning as "a partial fix is worse than none" from the 29 Aug comment, applied to a different thing.

Both are cases where a guard looked right and wasn't, which is the recurring theme on this issue:

- **The first cache guard passed a mutation it should have caught.** It opened all four apps and counted caches — but the app that activates *first* finds nothing to delete, so an unscoped filter there goes unnoticed. Every new guard is mutation-tested: re-adding a local `esc()`, breaking the import path, wiring an unknown `data-action`, commenting a key out inside a block comment, putting an inline handler back in vehicle, and unscoping each of the four workers.

The grocery suite **did** run and pass this time — `deploy.yml`'s test job is gated on grocery-related changes and `grocery/sw.js` was touched. - A deliberately failing test blocks the deploy
- An untouched app's suite is skipped, and the skip does not block anything
- Publishing an ordinary content change still deploys without waiting on browser tests

## Size

Normal

## Anything else?

**Needs an attended session.** This edits `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, which the nightly routine is forbidden to touch. Labelled `hold` — remove it and run `/backlog-work` on this yourself once GAP-W2 is done.

comments.body:
## Plan

Copying the grocery pattern exactly, as the issue asks: one change-detection job, one gated test job per app, and a `deploy` that fails closed.

**Files touched:** `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` only, plus a new regression test.

### The shape

- `changes` grows from one output to four (`grocery`, `bank_bonus`, `pool`, `vehicle`). Same fail-closed base-commit handling, same `workflow_dispatch` → run everything.
- Three new jobs — `test_bank_bonus`, `test_pool`, `test_vehicle` — mirroring `test` (which stays grocery's), each with its own working directory, `npm ci`, Playwright chromium, and screenshot + report artifacts.
- `deploy` gains all three to `needs`, each with the same `!= 'failure'` treatment so a skipped suite passes and a red one blocks.

### Two things I had to interpret

The issue says "copy grocery's pattern exactly." Grocery's current filter is missing two paths, and I'm fixing them here rather than replicating the gap four times:

1. **`tests/shared/**` is absent** — flagged in #109's closing note. An edit to the shared mock can currently skip every suite that depends on it, and a skipped job counts as a pass. Goes into grocery, bank-bonus and pool (vehicle doesn't use the mock).
2. **`quartz/static/shared/**` is absent** — this one wasn't flagged and is the bigger hole. GAP-W5 (#111) landed the shared data layer *after* grocery's filter was written. Grocery now imports seven files from it; pool and vehicle import `text.js`; bank-bonus imports `text.js` via `/static/shared/`. So today, editing `quartz/static/shared/dom.js` deploys to all four apps **with no suite running at all**. Goes into all four filters.

### Ports

5173 grocery / 5175 bank-bonus / 5176 pool / 5177 vehicle, already set in each `playwright.config.js`. Separate runners, so no collision either way.

### Before wiring

Running all four suites locally first. #109 pinned two `test.fail()` tests to track GAP-W4 (#112); #112 has since closed and those pins were already rewritten into direct assertions, so I expect green — but wiring a red suite into the deploy gate would block every publish, so this gets verified, not assumed.

### Not in scope

`tests/install-checks/` is also unwired. It isn't one of the three apps this issue names — separate item if you want it.

## Built, PR open, not merged — one decision for you

[#131](https://github.com/BarkernotBob/BarkernotBob.github.io/pull/131) has the work. Every "Done when" line is checked below. I stopped short of merging, for a reason worth a sentence.

### Done when

- [x] **Each app's suite runs in CI only when that app's files, its tests, or the workflow changed** — asserted by executing the filter, not by reading it: `quartz/static/pool/index.html` → `["pool"]`, `tests/vehicle/boot.spec.js` → `["vehicle"]`, two apps in one commit → exactly those two.
- [x] **A deliberately failing test blocks the deploy** — a failed matrix leg makes `needs.test.result == 'failure'`, and `deploy`'s condition requires `!= 'failure'`. Mutating that condition turns the suite red.
- [x] **An untouched app's suite is skipped, and the skip does not block anything** — nothing selected → `apps=[]` → `test` skipped → `deploy` still runs, because the condition is `!= 'failure'` and not `== 'success'`.
- [x] **Publishing an ordinary content change still deploys without waiting on browser tests** — `content/notes/some-note.md` → `[]`, no browser job at all.

### Two things I fixed that weren't in the issue

`quartz/static/shared/` was not in the grocery filter. GAP-W5 (#111) landed those modules after the filter was written, and all four apps import from them — so since #111, editing `quartz/static/shared/dom.js` shipped every app with nothing run against it. That's now a force-all path. `tests/shared/` was missing too, which #109 had already flagged.

Copying grocery's pattern verbatim would have reproduced both gaps three more times.

### Verification

All four suites green locally before wiring: grocery 106, bank-bonus 39, pool 54, vehicle 50.

The regression suite is mutation-checked — drop a path, an app, or the fail-closed condition and it goes red. Worth saying explicitly given #109 left two `test.fail()` pins that reported green while asserting nothing.

### 🔵 Why I didn't merge

**This PR has no CI.** All three checks report `skipping`: `deploy.yml` triggers only on push to `main`, and these paths don't match `backlog-checks.yml`'s filter. So the merge itself is the first execution of the new gate.

Worst case is recoverable — a broken `deploy.yml` blocks future publishes rather than taking the live site down, and a revert fixes it — but it wants someone watching the run rather than a fire-and-forget merge. Say the word and I'll merge and watch it.

`/code-review` was not run: CLAUDE.md says never unless you ask for it by name, and `/backlog-work` asking on its own behalf doesn't count.

Leaving this `in-progress`.

- [ ] `tests/pool/`
- [ ] `tests/vehicle/`

- Each of the three apps has its own suite under `tests/`
- Every suite passes against the app as it stands today
- `mock-github.js` exists once, in `tests/shared/`, used by all four suites
- The grocery suite still passes unchanged

From the 2026-07-12 audit (`AUDIT-GAPS.md`, GAP-W1). Priority **P1** — this one can break the live site with a green build.

## What do you want changed, and why?

The Quartz build gets two patches applied to it by hand: search tokenizing (`tokenize:"forward"` → `"full"`) and the explorer breakpoint (`800px` → `99999px`, which is load-bearing for the home page drawer). Those patches are written three separate times, as `sed` commands, in `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, `Publish Changes.command`, and `Preview Website.command`.

`sed` does nothing and reports success when it can't find what it's looking for. So the day an upstream Quartz update changes that generated file, the patches silently stop applying — the build goes green, the site deploys, and search and the home page are quietly broken. Three copies also means they can drift apart, which is how local preview and the live site end up different.

`patch-plugins.mjs` already does this correctly: it marks what it has patched so re-running is safe, it copes with renamed variables, and it says "anchor not found, left unchanged" out loud.

## Done when...

- No `sed`-based plugin patching remains anywhere in the repo
- All three entry points (deploy workflow, Publish, Preview) call the one shared script
- Deliberately breaking an anchor makes the GitHub Actions build **fail**, not pass quietly
- After a real deploy: site search still finds partial words, and the home page drawer still opens

## Size

Normal

**Needs an attended session.** This edits `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, which the nightly routine is forbidden to touch. Labelled `hold` so the nightly skips it cleanly — remove the label and run `/backlog-work` on it while you're awake.

BarkernotBob/logos-notes.body:
When two neighbouring bits of text in a Logos note have different formatting (for example bold, then bold+italic), the Obsidian copy shows stray asterisks: `**Significance*****:***` displays as **Significance** followed by a literal `***:***`.

Measured across all 539 live notes: 4 notes plus 1 sermon are affected:
- John 2.1 "Context of Chapter 2"
- Matthew 8.3 "Leprosy in the bible"
- James 1.12–18 "Outline"
- Genesis 6.5 "The following is the extract…"
- Sermon "The Gospel Mystery of Sanctification"

This bug is older than issue 34. Issue 34 fixed a different problem, the `****` double-wrap. Likely fix: use an unambiguous form (HTML tags) for these boundaries rather than more marker juggling. See `issues/34-paragraph-formatting-readdown.md` (Out of scope section).

comments.body:
**Nightly pass: plan**

Cause: the reader (`src/lib/xaml.ts`) wraps each Logos run in its own asterisks. It only merges two runs when the markers are identical, so bold `**Significance**` followed by bold-italic `***:***` gives `**Significance*****:***`, which Obsidian can't parse.

Fix, as the issue suggests: when two differently formatted runs touch with no space between them, write the second one with HTML tags (`<b>`, `<i>`, `<b><i>`) instead of asterisks. Every other case keeps its current output, so only the affected notes change.

Publishing has to read those tags back as well. Otherwise an edited note would publish literal `<b>` text into Logos. `src/lib/publish.ts` will accept exactly those tags and nothing more, the same narrow way it already handles `<sup>`.

Done when:
- Bold next to bold-italic, italic next to bold, and the other mixed pairs read down with no stray asterisks, and Obsidian would show the formatting.
- Publishing that markdown gives back the same bold/italic runs, and a second round trip changes nothing.
- A regression test covers both directions and runs in `npm test`.

Files: `raycast-logos-sync/src/lib/xaml.ts`, `src/lib/publish.ts`, a new `test/mem/mixed-emphasis.test.ts`, `package.json` (test script), and the issue file.

**What you asked for**

Warn when sync hasn't run for a while: the Sep 10 Raycast upgrade silently wiped the extension's preferences and hourly sync did nothing from Sep 9 to Sep 23 with no sign. The extension should surface a visible warning when the last successful sync is stale (e.g. >1 day). Small.

comments.body:
Nightly pass (2026-09-24): not built. Moving to `needs-grilling` because the issue doesn't say where the warning should show, and the code shows a problem that decides it.

**What I found in the code**
- `vaultPath` is a **required** extension-level preference (`package.json`). When the Sep 10 upgrade wiped it, Raycast stopped launching **every** command in the extension, including the hourly sync. So no code inside the extension could have run to warn you. A warning inside a command would not have caught this failure.
- Sync already writes its result to the **Sync Logos Notes** subtitle in Raycast search ("… · <date>" when it works, "Last sync failed — …" when it fails). That only helps if you look at it. If the command never runs, the subtitle just keeps showing the last good date.
- Search Notes & Documents doesn't show sync status anywhere.

**Questions (each has my recommended answer)**
1. **Where should the warning appear?** Recommended: a macOS notification, at most once a day while sync is stale, plus a warning row at the top of **Search Notes & Documents** for when you open it. The notification is the only option that reaches you when you aren't opening the extension.
2. **Should vault path stop being "required", so Raycast keeps running sync after a preference wipe and sync can tell you "Vault not set, sync is off"?** Recommended: yes. Without this change, the Sep 9–23 failure stays silent however the warning is built. Downside: a new install shows that error instead of Raycast's setup form.
3. **What does "a while" mean?** Recommended: more than 24 hours since the last *successful* sync. A sync that runs but fails, or gets skipped, still counts as stale.
4. **When does the warning go away?** Recommended: on its own after the next successful sync. No dismiss button, so it can't be silenced while sync is still broken.

Answer by number (for example "1 yes, 2 yes, 3 yes, 4 yes") and the next run can build it.

# Issue 15 — Scale-safe sync: chunked gathering + image failure cache

Label: `ready-for-agent`
Status: ready-for-agent
Blocked by: 14 (both edit the sync core — sequence to avoid collision).

## Parent

PRD-reliability-hardening.md (Implementation Decisions: "Chunked gathering", "Image
failure cache").

## What to build

Make sync survive very large libraries and dead image links without failing or stalling.

- **Chunked gathering.** Replace whole-library gathering with per-kind, id-ranged
  chunked queries that feed the existing incremental index update. This bounds memory
  and per-process pipe size regardless of library size (no more O(library) load / 256MB
  maxBuffer risk).
- **Image failure cache.** Persist failed image URLs with a retry-after backoff so every
  hourly sync isn't stalled ~20 s per dead link. Image fetching uses a small parallel
  pool and an overall per-run time budget, so the index update always gets its turn.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An oversized-library scenario syncs without exhausting memory or hitting the pipe/
      maxBuffer limit (assert it completes and indexes all kinds).
- [ ] Gathering is per-kind and id-ranged, feeding the incremental index update.
- [ ] A dead image URL is remembered and retried with backoff — not re-fetched (and
      re-stalled) every run; image fetching respects a per-run time budget.
- [ ] Regression test for the chunking (oversized-library) scenario.
- [ ] Build + lint + full test suite green; live extension reinstalled.
- [ ] Manual test written into this file on completion.

## Blocked by

- Issue 14 (sync safety guardrails) — both edit the sync core; land 14 first.

comments.body:
Nightly backlog pass: **this was already built and is on `main`** — the GitHub issue was just never closed. No code was written tonight. (Its stated blocker, issue #3 / slice 14, is also done.)

The local slice file left its acceptance boxes unticked, so I checked each against the code and the suite rather than taking the status line's word for it. **All hold:**

- **Chunked gathering** — `test/mem/chunked-sync.test.ts` passes 2/2, including `chunked sync indexes ALL kinds/notes at 10× without exhausting memory` (the oversized-library scenario) and a 1× check that every note still gets indexed.
- **Image failure cache** — `src/lib/image-cache.ts` persists failed URLs to `image-failures.json` with a retry-after backoff; `src/lib/sync-core.ts` fetches through a small parallel pool (`mapPool`) under a per-run wall-clock budget (`IMAGE_TIME_BUDGET_MS`, 60 s), after which remaining images hotlink so the index write still gets its turn.

**One acceptance line I can't tick from a cloud session:** the live extension reinstall (`ray` only runs on your Mac). Run `cd raycast-logos-sync && npm run dev`, wait for `ready - built extension successfully`, then stop the watcher.

## Manual test (for Isaiah)

1. Open Raycast → run **Sync Logos Notes** on your real library. It should complete without an error, a hang, or a "maxBuffer"/out-of-memory failure — even as the library grows (gathering now streams the library in bounded chunks instead of loading it all at once).
2. Watch the Sync command subtitle — it should finish with a normal `search index: N changed, M unchanged` line (no "FAILED").
3. **Dead image link doesn't stall every sync:** if you have a note/clipping referencing an image URL that no longer loads, run Sync twice in a row. The **second** Sync should NOT pause ~20 s again on that same dead link — the failed URL is remembered and skipped (retried only after a backoff), so sync stays quick.
4. Confirm all your note kinds still appear in Search after the sync (nothing dropped by the chunked gathering).

If any of that doesn't hold, reopen this issue and say which step failed.

## What to build

A cluster of small, independent correctness fixes. Each is tiny; grouped as one grabbable
slice.

- **Composite dedupe keys.** Index-hit dedupe and list keys use kind + id, never id
  alone, so results from different document kinds that share an id both appear (no silent
  overwrite).
- **Session-scoped count caching.** Kind counts for the search dropdown compute once per
  command mount (keyed on index path), not per keystroke, so typing stays snappy.
- **Deep-link escaping.** Titles embedded in Logos deep links are URL-encoded, including
  semicolons (e.g. a sermon titled "Grace; Faith" gets a working open-in-Logos link).
- **Safe truncation.** Filename truncation is surrogate-pair-aware, so a title ending in
  emoji never produces an invalid filename.
- **Rendered-text search matching.** Queries containing quotes/punctuation that span
  formatting boundaries match against the rendered text, so visible text is always
  findable.
- **Source hygiene.** Replace the literal NUL byte in the indexer source with its escape
  sequence, so a formatter/editor can't silently corrupt the indexer.

- [ ] Dropdown kind counts compute once per mount, not per keystroke.

Label: `ready-for-agent`

before or with the discovery change, since discovery changes are exactly when a
wrong-database pick is most likely — so they ship together.

## What to build

Make sync safe under machine variance and contention. Three cohesive guardrails:

- **Tombstone guardrail.** If a run would tombstone more than a threshold (10% of
  managed files, with a minimum absolute floor), it tombstones nothing that run and
  reports why. An owner preference can override when a mass deletion is genuinely
  intended.
- **Sync lock.** A lockfile in the extension's support directory prevents overlapping
  sync runs (e.g. a manual sync during the hourly one). A stale lock — older than a
  run's plausible duration — is broken automatically.
- **Database discovery.** Among candidate notestool databases (Logos + Verbum, all
  profile dirs), prefer the **most recently modified/active**, not the largest. The
  chosen database path appears in sync output.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A run that would tombstone >threshold (e.g. 50%) of managed files tombstones
      nothing and reports that the guardrail tripped (assert external behavior).
- [ ] The override preference lets an intended mass deletion proceed.
- [ ] A second sync started while one holds the lock does not run; a stale lock is
      broken automatically.
- [ ] Discovery picks the most-recently-active database; the chosen path is shown in
      sync output.
- [ ] Regression tests for the tombstone-cap (wrong/partial database) scenario and
      discovery ordering.
- [ ] Build + lint + full test suite green; live extension reinstalled.
- [ ] Manual test written into this file on completion.

**What you asked for**

A video from my subscriptions was skipped from being added to the hub page. It was a video from WardonWords, and the video was a collaboration between him and Reformed Baptist Network. My hunch is it's a big related to pulling in collab videos? URL: https://youtu.be/-X4ZD3fisSs?si=ut3JSima1cyzDnUy

comments.body:
Nightly pass, 2026-09-24: **not built. Moved to `needs-grilling`.** I found the cause, but fixing it means choosing a behaviour, and that choice is yours.

**Why it happened (from the code; YouTube was unreachable from the build machine tonight)**

- The hub gets new videos by checking each subscribed channel's RSS feed (a short "latest uploads" list that YouTube publishes for every channel) (`feedUrl` / `parseChannelFeed` in `src/subscriptions.ts`). That list only contains videos **uploaded by that channel**.
- `-X4ZD3fisSs` was uploaded by **Reformed Baptist Network**, with Ward on Words as the collaborator. RBN is not one of your subscribed channels, so no feed the hub checks ever listed this video. Nothing was dropped, because the video never came in.
- This is the same video and the same diagnosis recorded on 2026-08-06 (`docs/archive/HANDOFF-history-2026-09.md`, and the notes in issues 045 and 048). At that time the fix was "subscribe to RBN". You filed it again, so I'm reading that as: you want collab videos to show up without subscribing to the other channel. The questions below assume that.

**One lead worth knowing about:** account sync (desktop only, uses your signed-in cookies, runs every 12 hours) can already read your YouTube **subscription feed** (`:ytsubs`). That is the same list youtube.com/feed/subscriptions shows you. Today it's only a fallback, and only used to collect channel IDs (`src/main.ts` ~1748). YouTube's collaborations feature is meant to put a collab video in the subscription feed of everyone subscribed to *any* channel on it. If that holds, reading that feed on every sync would catch this video. I couldn't confirm it tonight.

**Blocking questions (each has my recommendation):**

1. **Should collab videos show up without you subscribing to the other channel?**
   Recommended: **yes**. Otherwise this issue is just 045 (a Subscribe button) and should be closed as covered by it.

## The problem

Specced tickets live as local markdown (`issues/NN-*.md`) in each repo, while the backlog lives in GitHub Issues. Two trackers means two places to look, and the local ones have free-text statuses ("Built 2026-08-31 — awaiting…", "CODE COMPLETE (pending human t…", ~130 with no status line). The Dev Hub should read GitHub only.

## The change

- Move every local ticket into a GitHub issue in its own repo, then retire the `issues/` folders. Specs stay as `docs/specs/<slug>.md`.
- Repos with local tickets today: blockchain, logos-notes, obsidian-ytfree, obsidian-passage-backlinks, theology-claim-map, ultrasearch.
- Status mapping (decided 2026-10-11): rewrite every status into the fixed vocabulary first, then map to labels. Anything "awaiting Isaiah's test" older than 30 days becomes done (closed); newer ones get a test label.
- Point the pipeline at GitHub: the "Issue tracker" section of `claude/CLAUDE.md` here, so `/to-tickets`, `/implement` and `/implement-spec` publish to and read from GitHub Issues.

## Questions for Isaiah

1. **Should the nightly build specced tickets?** Any open unlabelled issue is buildable, so migrated "Scoped, not built" tickets (~70 in theology-claim-map alone) would start getting built overnight.
   ➡️ Migrated not-built tickets land as `hold`, and you release a spec when you want it. New specs from here on land unlabelled, so the nightly builds them in Blocked-by order (replacing `/implement-spec` runs). Cost: new specs start building the first night after `/to-tickets` unless you hold them.
2. **Blocked-by edges.** ➡️ Use GitHub's native issue dependencies; the nightly skips any issue with an open blocker. Cost: the nightly's search query alone can't see blockers, so it checks each candidate.
3. **Test bucket.** ➡️ New `needs-test` label in `labels.json`; the nightly treats it like `needs-grilling` (don't build). Pass closes the issue; Fail removes the label and comments what broke.
4. **Already-done local tickets.** ➡️ Migrate them as closed issues, so a project's history shows up in the Dev Hub. Cost: a few hundred closed issues created in one go (notifications muted while it runs).
5. **Grouping by spec.** ➡️ One GitHub milestone per spec, linking to the spec file. Cost: none visible beyond a milestone field on each issue.

### What's the idea?

I want to be able to put in the big things that are going to need replacing and when — "roof in X years", "flooring", "vehicle replacement" — and have the workbook turn that list into what I need to be saving.

So: a list of long-term house/vehicle projects, each with a rough cost and a rough year, and out the other end a number that tells me what I need to be putting away per month to be ready for them. The forecast is the point — I want to see the lumpy stuff coming far enough out that it changes my savings rate today instead of surprising me.

### What's annoying you right now?

Nothing in the workbook plans for this. The budget handles the recurring month, and `Projection` handles 30-year net worth, but neither answers "the roof is 8 years old, what should I be setting aside." Right now these are things I know about in my head and they only become real when they break.

---

<sub>Context for the grilling chat, from the repo — not decisions:</sub>

- This is the 1–5+ year lumpy-capital gap. `docs/planning-v2-scope.md` Q6 set the planning horizon at 1–5 years with the next 12 months primary, and Feature B's `Cal Events` recurrence list tops out around a rolling 12 months — a roof 8 years out has no home in it today.

Question is whether this is a new sheet feeding both, or a horizon extension of `Cal Events`.
- Things worth being asked: is the output a **required monthly contribution** (sinking fund per item, funded or not), or just a dated wall of future cash needs? Do replacement costs inflate between now and the year they land? Does the fund draw from cash, or is it a tracked earmark inside existing balances? Does an item's remaining life get entered as a year, or as age + expected lifespan?
- Vehicles specifically already exist in two places — the `Vehicles` bucket with a `Vehicle depreciation / yr` input on `Projection`, and the Sienna loan whose real rate/term were never in the workbook (v1 open item). A vehicle *replacement* plan should connect to those, not become a third copy.
- The new-house BLOCKER in `docs/planning-v2-scope.md` sits upstream of the dollar figures here: roof/flooring ages belong to whichever house is actually owned.

## Grilled 2026-09-01 — sharpened spec

Seven forks put to Isaiah, all answered. This replaces the loose description above as the build target.

### Decisions

| # | Question | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | What comes out the other end? | **Per-item sinking fund with progress.** Each item gets its own required monthly number and a saved-so-far line; they sum to one total. Not a single blended figure, not a bare forecast. |
| 2 | Where does "saved so far" live? | **Notional earmark inside existing cash.** No new bank account. Isaiah types the amount he considers set aside; the sheet carves cash into *spoken for* vs *actually free*. |
| 3 | Do costs inflate? | **Yes — one global rate** in a single input cell, applied to every item out to its year. |
| 4 | How is an item entered? | **Cost + replacement year, typed directly.** No age/lifespan columns, no computed year. |
| 5 | Where does it live? | **A new sheet, `Big Ticket`.** Not an extension of `Cal Events`, and explicitly **not** columns on `Projection` (Q12: keep, demote, do not touch — `IRA` and `CoastFire` point at it and breakage doesn't undo). |
| 6 | Vehicles? | **A normal row.** "Van replacement, $28,000, 2031" behaves exactly like the roof. No trade-in column, no wiring to `Projection`'s `Vehicles` bucket or its depreciation rate, no dependency on the still-missing Sienna rate/term. |
| 7 | Certain vs maybe? | **No status column.** One list, one total. If an item is unsure, it stays off the sheet. (Deliberately declines to mirror `Cal Events`' Confirmed/Planned/Considering.) |
| 8 | Wait for `Cash Flow`? | **No — stands alone now.** `Cash Flow` doesn't exist yet; `Big Ticket` reads cash from `Balances` itself. Feeding the earmark into `Cash Flow` is a separate issue for later. |

### Sheet shape

```
BIG TICKET — what's coming, and what to set aside for it

Inflation rate      3.0%          ← the one dial

Item              Cost today  Year   Months  Cost then   Saved    Still need   Per month
Roof                 $12,000   2034      99    $16,127   $1,040      $15,087        $152
Flooring              $8,000   2029      39     $9,246     $600       $8,646        $222
Van replacement      $28,000   2031      63    $33,398       $0      $33,398        $530
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
                                                                TOTAL PER MONTH:    $904

Cash on hand (live from Balances)   $18,400
Earmarked for the above             -$1,640
────────────────────────────────────────────
Actually free                       $16,760
```

### The math, pinned down

- An item is assumed due at the **end** of its replacement year. `Months = (Year − YEAR(TODAY()))*12 + (12 − MONTH(TODAY()))`, floored at 1 so a past or current year can't divide by zero.
- `Cost then = Cost today × (1 + rate) ^ (Months / 12)`.
- `Still need = MAX(0, Cost then − Saved)` — an over-funded item shows $0 needed, never a negative monthly.
- `Per month = Still need / Months`.
- A row whose year has already passed shows **"due now"** and puts the whole remaining amount into the monthly column rather than hiding it.
- Blank rows contribute nothing and show nothing.
- `Cash on hand` reads live: `=VLOOKUP("CASH", Balances!$B$9:$D$250, 3, FALSE)` — the same source `Projection!C6` already uses.

### Done when…

- [ ] `scripts/build_big_ticket.py` exists and writes a new `Big Ticket` sheet into `Tiller Budget.xlsx`, following the repo's existing `build_*.py` conventions.
- [ ] The sheet has **20 blank item rows**, each taking Item name, Cost today, Replacement year, and Saved so far as typed inputs in cream input cells per `docs/format-standards.md`.
- [ ] A single **inflation rate** input cell sits above the table, in `0.0%` format, defaulting to `3.0%`.
- [ ] Months, Cost then, Still need and Per month are **formulas, not typed values**, and recalculate when any input changes.
- [ ] A **TOTAL PER MONTH** cell sums the per-item monthly column.
- [ ] A three-line block shows **Cash on hand** (live from `Balances`, read-only), **Earmarked** (the sum of Saved so far, shown negative), and **Actually free** (the difference).
- [ ] Currency cells use `$#,##0.00` and the rate cell uses `0.0%`.
- [ ] An item whose replacement year has passed reads **"due now"** and still contributes its full remaining amount to the total.
- [ ] Over-funding an item yields `$0` still needed and `$0` per month — never a negative number.
- [ ] `Projection`, `Balances`, `IRA` and `CoastFire` are **not modified**. The only cross-sheet reference is one read-only VLOOKUP into `Balances`.
- [ ] `scripts/verify_big_ticket.py` exists and checks the sheet opens with no formula errors, matching the existing `verify_*.py` pattern.
- [ ] `docs/planning-v2-scope.md` gains a short section recording that the 5+ year lumpy-capital gap is now owned by `Big Ticket`, so it isn't re-specified into `Cal Events` later.

### Manual test (for Isaiah)

1. Open `Tiller Budget.xlsx` and find the new **Big Ticket** tab.
2. In the first empty row, type `Roof` for the item, `12000` for cost today, `2034` for the year, and leave Saved so far blank.
3. Check the row fills itself in: it should show roughly `$16,127` as the cost then and about `$152` a month. The exact pennies will differ depending on today's date — you're checking it's in the neighbourhood, not to the cent.
4. Type `1040` into Saved so far on that row. The per-month number should **drop** (to roughly `$137`).
5. Add two more rows — `Flooring`, `8000`, `2029` and `Van replacement`, `28000`, `2031`.
6. Check **TOTAL PER MONTH** near the bottom equals the three per-month numbers added up.
7. Change the inflation rate cell from `3.0%` to `6.0%`. Every "cost then" and every monthly number should jump. Put it back to `3.0%`.
8. Look at the bottom block. **Cash on hand** should match what the `Balances` tab says your cash is. **Earmarked** should be `-$1,040` (only the roof has anything saved). **Actually free** should be cash minus that.
9. Type `9999` into the Saved so far cell for the roof — more than it needs. Still needed should read `$0.00` and per month `$0.00`, not a negative. Clear it back to `1040`.
10. Change the roof's year to `2024` (in the past). The row should say **due now** and the total should jump. Change it back to `2034`.
11. Open the `Projection` tab and confirm it looks exactly as it did before — nothing on it should have changed.

### Explicitly out of scope

- Feeding the earmark or the monthly total into `Cash Flow` — that sheet doesn't exist yet; separate issue once it does.
- Any connection to `Projection`'s `Vehicles` bucket, its depreciation rate, or the Sienna loan.
- Trade-in values, per-item inflation rates, certain/maybe statuses, age-plus-lifespan entry.
- Automatically clearing an item once it's actually bought — for now Isaiah deletes the row himself.

### Not a blocker

The **new-house BLOCKER** in `docs/planning-v2-scope.md` does *not* hold this up. Costs and years are typed by hand rather than derived from house data, and the only live read is the cash balance. Roof and flooring estimates will want revisiting once the house question settles, but that's Isaiah editing two cells, not a rebuild.

Status: planned

Game: Blockchain (seen). Hex / Ball / Dodeca workers have the identical line — verify each.
Source: Isaiah, 1v1 vs bot, 2026-09-28

**What happened:** The bot paid 1 token and played a wild on a paid column. It should have paid 2 (1 wild + 1 column). When Isaiah tried the same thing, he was correctly charged 1 for the wild and then blocked from the paid column because he had no second token.

## Cause
- The worker builds wild and blocker candidates with `baseCost: 0` (`ai-worker.js:509`, `:522`; same in `ai-worker.hex.js`, `.ball.js`, `.dodeca.js`), even when the column is paid or locked. It also only checks `aiTokens >= rules.wildCost`, not wild + column.
- `main.js:~196` only charges the column when `chosenMove.baseCost > 0`, so the column toll is skipped.
- The column toll lives in the click handler (`main.js:~6572`, `~6624`), not in `commitMove`, so any programmatic path skips it. **Also check the online host path** — `_hostApplyMove` (`main.js:~4349`) charges only the purchase cost for wild/blocker, and `_hostRejectReason` doesn't count the column; a guest may be able to do the same thing online.

## Fix direction
- Worker: wild and blocker candidates carry the column's real `baseCost` (as standard moves do) and require `aiTokens >= purchaseCost + baseCost`. Timebomb/core: check whether a paid column should cost extra for them too and match the human rule.
- Better: move the column-toll charge and check into one shared place both humans and bots go through (or at least have the bot path and `_hostApplyMove` use the same helper), so the rule can't drift again.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A bot placing a wild or blocker on a paid/locked column pays purchase cost + column cost; it doesn't try when it can't afford both.
- [ ] Online: a guest's wild/blocker on a paid column is charged the same (or refused if unaffordable) by the host.
- [ ] Canaries: (a) bot wild on a paid column → tokens drop by wildCost + column cost; (b) bot with only wildCost tokens never picks a paid column for its wild; (c) host-applied wild intent on a paid column charges both.
- [ ] Build `--all`, `--fast` suite green, `tests/baseline.json` bumped.
