BarkernotBob/blockchain.body:
Status: planned
Size: Normal
Game: Blockchain (seen). Hex / Ball / Dodeca use copies of the same worker + the same shared `main.js` bot path, so they are very likely affected too. Verify each.
Source: Isaiah, 1v1 vs Bot level 10, 2026-09-28

**What happened:** Isaiah had a win the bot couldn't block. The bot laid a wild, then tried to win on the same turn (illegal). The toast "Illegal move: Cannot win on the same turn a wild is laid" showed, then the bot sat there and never moved again. The game was stuck.

## Two bugs
1. **The bot picks an illegal move.** After a wild, the worker re-thinks with `wildPlaced: true`. It skips the immediate-win shortcut (`ai-worker.js:339`), but the normal search and the fallback (`ai-worker.js:416`, `:632`) never drop placements that would complete the bot's own 4. A win still scores best, so it picks one.
2. **Nothing recovers when a bot move is refused.** `aiWorker.onmessage` (`main.js:~170`) sets `isAiThinking = false` and calls `commitMove`. `commitMove` refuses the move with a toast and `return`s (`main.js:7292`) without ending the turn or re-scheduling. It is still the bot's turn, no one schedules another think → frozen.

Related, same path: the bot deducts tokens BEFORE calling `commitMove` (`main.js:~246` for wild, same for blocker/lock/etc.). If `commitMove` then refuses (e.g. `Wild would create 4-in-a-row`, `main.js:7268`), the tokens are gone with nothing placed.

## Fix direction
- Worker (all four `ai-worker*.js`): when `wildPlaced`, filter out any placement that `checkWin` says would complete the bot's own line — in the standard search, the depth search and the fallback. Also don't offer a wild that would itself create a 4 for anyone (mirror `wouldCreateFourAnyPlayer`).
- `main.js` bot path: after applying a bot move, if it is still this bot's turn and the move didn't take (board/turn unchanged), refund any tokens it deducted, log it, and re-schedule with that move excluded (pass an `excludeMoves` list to the worker). Cap retries (e.g. 3); after that, fall back to any legal plain placement, or end the turn — never leave the game stuck.
- Consider a general bot watchdog: if a bot's turn has lasted N seconds with no think in flight, re-schedule it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] With a wild placed this turn, the bot never chooses a placement that completes its own line (all four workers).
- [ ] If any bot move is refused by `commitMove`, the bot's tokens are restored and it makes a different legal move (or ends its turn) within a few seconds — the game never stalls on the bot's turn.
- [ ] Canaries (square, plus hex/ball/dodeca where the path is shared): (a) set up a board where the bot's only winning cell becomes illegal after its wild → bot's next move is legal; (b) inject a refused bot move via `_aiDeliver` → turn still advances and tokens are unchanged.
- [ ] Build `--all`, `--fast` suite green, `tests/baseline.json` bumped.

The online simulation in the full test suite (`node tests/run-tests.mjs`, the `?onlinesim=1` step) sometimes fails 2–3 of its 64 checks, then passes 64/64 on a re-run.

Seen:
- 2026-07-19: 62/64, clean on re-run.
- 2026-09-23 (pre-publish run): 61/64, clean on re-run. Failing checks:
  `converge[guest-normal-r1] board :: host(5) != canon(4)` and `converge[guest-normal-r1] cur/turn :: canon 1/4 vs host 2/5`. The host ended up one move ahead of the canonical state in one guest round.

The real two-window Firebase game passed both times (host 15/15, guest 14/14, converged). So I don't know yet whether this is a timing problem in the simulation harness or a real sync bug that shows up rarely in real games.

Done when:
- The root cause is found: reproduce by looping the online sim, add logging around the guest-normal round, and identify it.
- It's either fixed with a canary, or shown to be a harness-only timing issue and the harness made deterministic.
- 10 consecutive online-sim runs pass 64/64.

comments.body: Also seen in **Hexchain** on 2026-09-23 (pre-publish run): 61/64, different round: `converge[after-undo] board :: host(3) != canon(5)` and `converge[after-undo] cur/turn :: canon 2/9 vs host 1/7`. So it isn't square-specific; the shared sync code or the shared sim harness is the likelier place to look.

Fixed in #49 (merged, eae1a85).

**Root cause:** this was a real sync bug, not just harness timing. The Firebase SDK runs one transaction per location at a time. When anything writes under the room, it aborts every *queued* room transaction with error `'set'`. Writes that do this include the host's `pendingMoves` `drop()`, a guest's intent push, and presence. `_hostApplyIntent` publishes twice and then calls `drop()`, so the second publish was sometimes discarded. The room then held the previous board and turn: `host(5) != canon(4)`, `canon 1/4 vs host 2/5`. `_firebaseSave` now re-publishes the current state when the newest publish is aborted. The fix has canaries in square and hex.

**Found on the way, all fixed with canaries or corrected checks:**
- **Regression harness:** `test()` counted a returned failure string as a pass, so `cond || 'why'` canaries could never fail. The wild and undo-purchase tests had been passing without testing anything.
- **Undo refunded purchases twice:** 10 → buy → 7 → undo → 13.
- **Bot hand-off stall:** a bot that inserted a core cancelled the next bot's scheduled turn, so the game stalled whenever two bots played in a row.
- **Two sim-only flakes:**
  - The undo check assumed the board shrinks, but a timebomb explosion can make it grow.
  - `waitFor` returned false without a final check when a main-thread stall pushed it past its deadline.

**Verification:** all runs used a local RTDB emulator, because the cloud environment can't reach firebaseio.com.
- Online sim: 10/10 consecutive runs at 67/67 (the sim grew from 64 to 67 checks).
- Regression: square 48/48, hex 64/64, ball 36/36, dodeca 64/64.
- Each new canary fails on a build without its fix.
- CI is green.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Root cause identified: the SDK aborts a queued transaction on a child write.
- [x] Fixed, with canaries (`publish abort (#39)`, `bot core hands the turn to the next bot (no stall)`).
- [x] The online sim convergence check is deterministic: it waits for publishes to settle instead of sleeping.
- [x] 10 consecutive online-sim runs are clean (67/67, emulator).
- [ ] One clean run against real Firebase (see below).

## Manual test (for Isaiah)
1. Open Terminal in `~/Projects/blockchain` and run `git pull`.
2. Run `node tests/run-tests.mjs` (the full run, **not** `--fast`). It takes a few minutes, and no windows open.
3. In the output, find the online sim line. It should say **67/67**. The two-window game should pass for both host and guest.
4. The regression line for Blockchain should say **48/48**.
5. Optional: run step 2 two more times. Every run should be clean. If any run shows fewer than 67/67, paste the failing lines into this issue and reopen it.

BarkernotBob/blockchain.body:
### What happens today
Found while verifying host failover (issue file 01) in real Chrome on 2026-09-22. With the default rules (Turn Timer off), once a player closes their window mid-game, the game waits on their seat forever the next time it's their turn — nobody else can move. The host-failover work keeps the game alive when the **host** leaves (a guest takes over, bots keep playing), but the departed player's own turn still stalls everyone. This applies to any player who leaves, host or guest.

Not tested: whether the Turn Timer rule, when it's on, moves the game past the empty seat.

### Decision (Isaiah, 2026-09-23)
The **host** decides. 30 seconds after a player disconnects, the host gets a prompt:
1. **Keep waiting**: asks again after another 30 seconds.
2. **Replace with a bot**: a bot plays their seat from now on (their pieces, tokens and score stay).
3. **Skip their turns**: their turns pass automatically (their pieces stay on the board).

Also:
- If the host is the one who left, host failover (item 01) makes a new host, and that host gets the prompt.
- Everyone sees a "disconnected" marker next to the player's name while they're gone, in a fixed slot (no reflow).
- A player who rejoins gets their seat back (the bot hands it back and skipping stops) and the prompt closes.

### Done when...
- [ ] The host sees the three-choice prompt 30 s after a player's presence drops, and not before.
- [ ] Keep waiting re-prompts after another 30 s. Bot and Skip both let the game continue past that seat.
- [ ] A rejoining player gets their seat back.
- [ ] After a host failover, the new host gets the prompt.
- [ ] Canaries: each of the three choices drives the real turn engine. Timers are injectable so tests don't wait 30 s.
- [ ] Build `--all`; fast suite green; one full real-Firebase run before publish.

> **19. O(board²) removal diffs** — `find()` inside per-cell loops; index by cell-key Map.

Status: planned
Blocked-by: —
Size: Quick
Game: all four (shared `main.js`)
Source: `OPTIMIZATION_PLAN.md` item 19, re-checked 2026-09-22

**Impact:** small. On a big board, each snapshot's removal pass scans every piece once per cell. The
bigger win is dedupe: the same "find the piece mesh at (cx, cz, lvl)" search is hand-written about
10 times with slightly different filters, so one of them getting it wrong is easy.

## Problem
`G.pieces.find(p => p.userData.type === 'piece' && p.userData.cx === … && … lvl === …)` appears at
`app/main.js` ~238, 253, 3024, 3117, 5350, 5573, 5591, 5651, 5676, 6511. The ones at ~3024 and ~3117
run inside per-cell loops in the snapshot handler.

## Fix direction
One `pieceAt(cx, cz, lvl)` helper, backed by a `Map` kept in sync wherever `G.pieces` gains or loses
a piece mesh (or rebuilt once per snapshot). Replace the hand-written searches. Same function as
issue #25's `setupListener` cleanup, so don't run the two in parallel.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] One piece-lookup helper; no hand-written `G.pieces.find(...cx...cz...lvl...)` left.
- [ ] Canary: after place → remove → undo, `pieceAt` returns the right mesh (or null) for each cell.
- [ ] Build `--all`; `--fast` green plus one `--all`; baseline bumped.

## Manual test (for Isaiah)
*(Written when the issue is completed — not before.)*

**What you asked for**

Status: planned

Size: Quick
Game: Blockchain (square); Ball if it uses the same geometry functions
Source: `OPTIMIZATION_PLAN.md` item 16, re-checked 2026-09-22 and narrowed to geometry only

**Impact:** each Blockchain piece builds its own rounded-box geometry, so memory use and build time
grow with every piece. Hex and Dodeca already share theirs. Small but free win, and it makes the games
consistent.

## Problem
`app/variant.square.js` ~112: `solidGeo()` returns `new RoundedBoxGeometry(PS, PS, PS, 4, 0.1)` on
every call. Hex/Dodeca cache it (`cachedSolidGeo`) and their disposer skips the cached geometry
(`variant.dodeca.js` ~264).

**Materials must NOT be shared.** Code elsewhere changes `.material.emissive` and `.opacity` on
individual pieces (see CLAUDE.md: "Piece meshes must stay MeshStandardMaterial"). A shared material
would make one piece's highlight or fade hit every piece of that colour. That part of the original
plan item is dropped.

## Fix direction
Cache `solidGeo()` (and `sliceGeo`/`ringGeo`/`coreInnerGeo` if they're never mutated) the way Hex
does, and have the dispose path skip cached geometry. `wildGeo()` stays unique (it has baked vertex
colours).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Two Blockchain pieces share one geometry object; the wild piece doesn't.
- [ ] Removing, undoing or exploding a piece never disposes the shared geometry (the next placed piece
      still renders).
- [ ] Canaries in `variant.square.js` mirroring Hex/Dodeca's (`wild uses its OWN … geometry` and
      "shared geo survives removal"). Fail before the fix.
- [ ] Build `--all`; tests green; baseline bumped.

*(Written when the issue is completed — not before.)*

**What you asked for**
> **4. Full-state writes on every move (biggest latency win)** — `_firebaseSave` transacts the ENTIRE
> room; `serializeState` embeds unbounded `history`; the transaction return re-writes `chat` and
> `pendingMoves` too. Every move re-uploads/downloads the whole room — latency and bandwidth grow with
> game age and chat length. Fix: multi-path `update()` deltas (changed cells + bounded move log); move
> chat and history out of the move path; cap history.
> — `OPTIMIZATION_PLAN.md` item 4

Status: planned — run alone; needs a heavy two-window run
Blocked-by: —
Size: Big
Game: all four (shared sync code)
Source: `OPTIMIZATION_PLAN.md` item 4, re-checked 2026-09-22

**Impact:** every online move uploads the whole room, including all chat and the full undo history
(each entry carries a copy of the turn state). A move late in a chatty game costs far more than the
first move, which on phone connections shows up as lag between tapping and the other player seeing it.

## Problem
`window._firebaseSave` (`app/main.js` ~3339) runs `gameRef.transaction` and returns
`Object.assign({}, current, payload, {seq})`. A transaction uploads the whole node, and `chat`
(`gameRef.child('chat')`, ~2921) and `pendingMoves` live under that node. `serializeState` includes
`history` with no cap (`app/serialize.js` ~49).

## Fix direction
Keep the atomic seq transaction (it's what makes sync exactly-once — see plan "Strengths"), but shrink
what it covers. Full multi-path deltas are riskier and not needed for the main win.
1. Split the room: the transaction covers a `state` child only; `chat`, `pendingMoves` and presence
   sit beside it.
2. Cap `history` in the synced payload (e.g. the last N turns — agree on N with Isaiah, since it
   bounds online undo depth).
3. Bump `schemaVersion`; old rooms fall back to (or are migrated from) the current shape.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Payload per move stays roughly flat over a 60-move game with 30 chat messages. Measure the
      transaction payload size at move 5 and move 60.
- [ ] Canary: the serialized payload has no `chat`/`pendingMoves` and `history.length` ≤ the cap.
- [ ] Online sim (`?onlinesim=1`) and the two-window real-Firebase game both pass (one heavy run).
- [ ] Undo still works online up to the cap.

## Manual test (for Isaiah)
*(Written when the issue is completed — not before.)*

comments.body:
**Nightly progress (2026-09-29)**

Plan:
- New rooms use layout v3 (`SCHEMA_VERSION` 3). The seq transaction covers only `games/<id>/state`. Chat, pending moves, presence and the lobby fields sit beside it, so a move no longer uploads them.
- History moves out of the transaction into `games/<id>/historyLog`, one entry per child. Each publish writes only the entries that changed (usually 1 new entry, or a few nulls after an undo). `state.historyLen` says how many entries are live.
- **I'm not capping history.** Once history is out of the move path, a cap isn't needed for flat uploads, so there's no N to agree on. Online undo keeps its full depth, and so do the game-end replay and the ML record.
- `roomView()` folds `state` + `historyLog` back into the old flat shape, so the snapshot listener and the test harnesses read it unchanged. The root `host` stays the authority for who is host, because only failover's claim transaction writes it.
- Rooms already in play (v2) keep the old whole-room write. If database rules refuse the new paths, the host falls back to the whole-room write.
- Canaries in all four games drive the real `_firebaseSave` and the real snapshot listener against an in-memory fake room: upload size over 60 moves + 30 chat messages, rebuilding a client, undo at depth, stand-ins (#37), failover, the v2 room path and the rules fallback.
- Files: `app/serialize.js`, `app/main.js`, `app/variant.*.js`, `tests/baseline.json`.

Status: planned

Size: Quick
Game: all four (shared `main.js`)
Source: `OPTIMIZATION_PLAN.md` item 20, re-checked 2026-09-22 and upgraded from perf polish to a bug

**Impact:** online games that use paid columns, locks or Add a Column leak GPU memory on **every
snapshot**, for every such column. Long games degrade on phones, the same way the chain-link leak
(plan item 3, fixed) did.

## Problem
Found by reading the code (not measured yet). After every snapshot, the listener calls
`updateColumnLabel` for **every** footprint column (`app/main.js` ~3174–3179).
`updateColumnLabel` (~5220) removes the old label group with `scene.remove(oldGroup)` but never
disposes it, then builds a new one. Each rebuild allocates a canvas + `CanvasTexture` +
`SpriteMaterial` (`createCostSprite`, ~5194). For locked or newly added columns it also allocates new
padlock/chain geometries (`buildChainsAndLocks`, ~5068).

## Fix direction
1. Dispose the old group's geometries and sprite texture/material before dropping it. **Don't** dispose
   the shared `mats.iron`/`mats.steel`/`mats.black` materials from `constants.js`.
2. Only rebuild a column's label when its inputs change (cost, lock count, newly-added, top level).
   Keep a small per-column signature and skip unchanged columns.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Canary in `variantTests` (every variant — shared code): set up a paid + locked column, call the
      snapshot label path 20×, and assert `renderer.info.memory.textures` / `.geometries` don't grow.
      Fails before the fix.
- [ ] Labels still show the right cost, lock chains and padlocks after lock, unlock, add and remove.
- [ ] `node app/build.mjs --all`; `node tests/run-tests.mjs --fast` green plus one `--all`;
      `tests/baseline.json` bumped.

**On hold:** needs Isaiah's 2–3 visual reference images.

Note: needs Isaiah's visual reference target

Blocked by: nothing technical. Blocked on a human input (see "The blocker" below).

## Problem

The game reads as a cartoon toy, not a "professional, realistic" product. Isaiah wants the visual
design to be **"really intriguing."** A 2026-07-19 session tried four backdrop directions plus a
neutral studio sweep; Isaiah rejected all of them:

> "Those all look terrible. NONE of those is the quality I'm looking for."

Archived renders + full post-mortem: `docs/visual-explorations/README.md`.

## Root cause of the failed attempt (do not repeat)

Swapping only the **backdrop**, built from **procedural canvas gradients + primitive slabs**, has a
hard quality ceiling. The backdrop was never the main constraint:

- **Pieces cap perceived quality** — saturated primary red/blue `MeshStandardMaterial` cubes with
  baseline `emissiveIntensity 0.2` self-glow look like cheap plastic in every environment.
- **No HDRI** — canvas-gradient env maps give flat, synthetic reflections.
- **No post-processing** — no `EffectComposer` anywhere; no bloom, SSAO, DoF, or colour grading, so
  nothing feels grounded or physically present.
- **No art direction** — themes were agent guesses with no target reference.

## The blocker

**Isaiah must supply 2–3 reference images** showing the quality/vibe he wants (screenshots of other
games, product renders, art direction boards — anything concrete). Every further attempt without a
target is another guess, and guessing has now failed twice (audit-session mockups, then this).

Ask him: realistic/photoreal? stylised-but-premium? dark and moody? bright and clean? Is the
**wooden-table-in-a-park framing** itself up for replacement, or is the table sacred?

## Scope when unblocked

Treat as ONE art direction, not four separate tickets — plan items 10 + 11 + 12 + 14 together:

- **10 — environment:** replace the procedural park. Use a real **HDRI** for IBL, not canvas gradients.
- **11 — piece materials:** kill the baseline `emissiveIntensity 0.2` self-glow (→ 0), roughness ~0.3,
  `envMapIntensity` ~1.2. ⚠️ **Materials must stay `MeshStandardMaterial`** — other code iterates
  every piece touching `.material.emissive`/`.opacity`; swapping the class caused cascading crashes
  before (CLAUDE.md).
- **12 — post-processing:** `EffectComposer` with subtle UnrealBloom + SSAO + SMAA, gated behind a
  quality toggle for mobile.
- **14 — palette/typography:** one display webfont; promote ad-hoc JS hex colours into `:root` vars /
  a JS palette constant.

Perf note: deleting the park's ~17k instanced draws is a real side-benefit; don't lose it by
replacing them with something equally heavy.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Isaiah has supplied a reference target, and the direction is agreed **before** implementation.
- [ ] Proposed look presented as **real Chrome/WebGL renders of the live game** (never flat mockups —
      that failure mode is why this issue exists) and explicitly signed off by Isaiah.
- [ ] Piece meshes are still `MeshStandardMaterial`; no crash/vanishing regressions.
- [ ] Post-processing is quality-gated so mobile/weak devices are not degraded.
- [ ] `node app/build.mjs --all` passes; `node tests/run-tests.mjs --fast` green; baselines reconciled
      in `tests/baseline.json` if any canary is added.
- [ ] Frame rate on the square variant is no worse than the park baseline.
- [ ] Other three variants (hex/ball/dodeca) still build and pass — shared `main.js` change.

## Manual test (for Isaiah)

*(Written when the issue is completed — not before, per project rules.)*

## Notes

- Prototype branch `proto/studio-backdrop` (commit `04808ad`) has the rejected themes behind
  `?bg=void|neon|cosmic|dusk`. Reference only — **never merge** (prototypes don't merge to main).
- Reusable real-Chrome screenshot recipe is in `docs/visual-explorations/README.md`; headless
  Chromium has no WebGL, so captures must use `channel: 'chrome', headless: false`.

**Blocked by #2** (same new-game code path) — don't start until #2 is closed.
Size: Normal
Game: all four (shared `main.js`)
Source: code-health review 2026-09-22

**Impact:** a second game in one page load starts with the first game's pieces still in the board
state. They're invisible and can't be undone, but they still occupy cells and can count toward lines.
Store items hidden in game 1 (e.g. Blocker) also stay hidden in game 2 even when enabled.

## Problem
Reproduced in real Chrome 2026-09-22: 6 pieces in game 1 → Main Menu → new local game → game 2
starts with `board=6`, `pieces=6`, `historyLen=0`. Blocker enabled in setup, but its store item
is still `display:none`.

Root cause:
- `returnToMainMenu()` (`app/main.js` ~1062) doesn't reset `G.board`, `G.pieces`, `G.over`,
  `G.winner` or `G.bombMeshes`, and doesn't clear `.action-wrap`.
- `startLocalGame()` resets history, locks and turnState only.
- The store refresh only ever sets disabled items to `display='none'`, never back.

## Fix direction
One `resetGameState()` used by every new-game path (local, online, tutorial, rematch): clear board,
pieces (dispose meshes), bombs, selection, over/winner, `.action-wrap`. Store refresh sets
visibility both ways.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] After Main Menu → new game, board and pieces are empty, `G.over` is false, no stray confirm UI.
- [ ] A store item enabled in game 2 is visible even if it was disabled in game 1.
- [ ] Canary in `variantTests` (every variant): place pieces, `returnToMainMenu()`, start a new local
      game, assert empty board/pieces and `over === false`. Fails before the fix.
- [ ] Build `--all`; tests green (`--fast` + one `--all`); baseline bumped.

## Manual test (for Isaiah)
*(Written when the issue is completed — not before.)*

comments.body:
Notes from the #2 fix (PR #62), for whoever picks this up:

- `initThree()` now keeps the renderer, camera, OrbitControls, input listeners and render loop for the whole page load. Each new game still gets a **fresh `scene`**, and the old scene's geometries, materials and textures are **disposed** (`_disposeScene`). So after #62, any old-game mesh still referenced from `G.pieces`, `G.bombMeshes`, `G.tileObjects`, `G.ghost`, `G.animations` etc. points into a dead scene with freed GPU buffers. That's harmless today (nothing re-adds them), but `resetGameState()` should just empty those arrays/maps. Don't `scene.remove` them from the new scene, and don't reuse them.
- Order matters: `startFromLobby` calls `initThree()` → `buildBoard()` **before** anything resets `G.board` / `G.pieces`. The reset belongs at the start of `startLocalGame()` / online start / tutorial / rematch, not inside `initThree`. If it goes after `buildBoard`, the stale `G.board` could still affect the first render/hover.
- The regression helpers `fresh()` in every `variant.*.js` hand-clear board/pieces/over/winner after `startFromLobby()`, which hides this bug the same way the hex/dodeca `initThree` guard hid #2. Your canary needs to check state **before** that manual clear (or skip `fresh()`), or it will pass without the fix.
- `window._threeStats()` (added in #62) returns `{bound, loops}` in case it's useful.

BarkernotBob/blockchain.body:
**Blocked by #1** (both edit `initThree` / the resize handler — avoid conflicting edits) — don't start until #1 is closed.
Size: Normal
Game: all four (shared `main.js`)
Source: code-health review 2026-09-22

**Impact:** anyone who plays a second game without reloading (Main Menu → new game, or tutorial →
real game) gets one tap = piece placed, **no confirm step**. Every extra game also adds another render
loop, so CPU and battery use keep climbing.

## Problem
Reproduced in real Chrome 2026-09-22. After game 2 in one page load: canvas pointerdown 2→4,
pointerup 1→2, wheel 2→4, window keydown 2→3, resize 1→2, and 240 frame callbacks/second. In game 1
a single tap selects a column (confirm button appears); in game 2 the same tap places the piece,
because `handleClick` runs twice.

Root cause: `initThree()` (`app/main.js` ~4241) creates a new Scene + WebGLRenderer, adds canvas
pointer/touch/wheel listeners and window keydown/resize listeners, and starts a new
`requestAnimationFrame` loop **every call**. Nothing tears the old ones down. It's called from
`startFromLobby` (~1541), which every new game goes through.

## Fix direction
Make `initThree` idempotent: create renderer, scene, listeners and the loop once; on later calls
only clear/rebuild the board contents. Preferred over a full teardown/rebuild because browsers cap
live WebGL contexts and a leaked context eventually breaks rendering.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Starting a second (and third) game in one page load leaves listener counts and the number of
      running loops unchanged.
- [ ] In game 2, a single tap selects and shows the confirm button (same as game 1).
- [ ] Canary in `variantTests` (every variant — shared code): drive the real new-game path twice,
      assert one loop and no added listeners. Fails before the fix.
- [ ] `node app/build.mjs --all`; `node tests/run-tests.mjs --fast` green, plus one `--all` run
      (shared code); `tests/baseline.json` bumped.
- [ ] Checked in real Chrome: two games back to back, tap behaviour identical.

## Manual test (for Isaiah)
*(Written when the issue is completed — not before.)*

---

comments.body:
**Plan (nightly pass, 2026-09-25)** — resuming; no prior notes or PR from the earlier pickup. #1 is closed (PR #57), so the blocker is gone.

- `app/main.js` `initThree()`: split into a once-only part (WebGLRenderer, camera, OrbitControls + its `change` listener, canvas pointer/touch/wheel listeners, window keydown/resize listeners, `initCamControls()` slider/button listeners, the `requestAnimationFrame` loop) and a per-game part (fresh Scene with background/tabletop/lights/grid/board, camera aspect + fit radius, orbit target/limits, camera angles). The old scene's geometries/materials get disposed when a new game replaces it, so GPU memory doesn't pile up either.
- Also found: `initCamControls()` was re-binding the rotate/height sliders and buttons each game (so ⟲/⟳ jumped 30° in game 2), and a new OrbitControls was stacking its own canvas listeners. Both are covered by the once-only guard.
- Hex/Dodeca regression suites wrap `initThree` with a "skip if renderer exists" test guard to dodge the WebGL context leak. That workaround hides this bug, so I'll remove it (keeping the analytics mute) so the canary drives the real path.
- Canary in all four `variant.*.js`: start two games back to back via the real lobby path; assert the renderer/camera/orbit are the same objects, no listeners were added to the canvas/window/camera controls on game 2, and exactly one render loop is running. `tests/baseline.json` bumped by 1 per variant.
- Not touching #3 (board/pieces carrying over) — I'll leave notes there.

**Done: merged in #62.**

**What changed:** `initThree()` now creates the WebGL renderer, camera, OrbitControls, the canvas/window input listeners, the camera slider/button listeners and the render loop **once per page load**. Each new game only rebuilds the scene: background, tabletop, lights and board. It also re-fits the camera and resets it to the default view. The replaced scene's geometries, materials, textures, shadow maps and baked sky env map are freed. The test-only "run initThree once" guard in the Hex/Dodeca suites is removed, because it hid this bug.

**How I verified it:** headless Chromium + SwiftShader. three.js/firebase came from npm copies, because this sandbox blocks jsdelivr/gstatic.
- `--fast` for each variant, after the build: square 55/55, hex 71/71, ball 41/41, dodeca 69/69. Sync self-test and console scan were clean on all four. CI (square, real Chrome) is green.

- Real tap test (1300×900): three games back to back in one page load, tapping the same tile each time.
  - Before the fix: game 1 selected, **game 2 placed a piece immediately** (board 0→1), game 3 carried it over.
  - After the fix: all three games select and show the action button with nothing placed, and `loops` stays 1.
  - Screenshot of game 2 shows the board, table and scenery rendering normally.
- After the whole ~55-game regression run in one page: still exactly 1 render loop.

**Acceptance criteria:** all met. "Checked in real Chrome" was done in headless Chromium, not Google Chrome, because Chrome can't be downloaded here. CI's real-Chrome run passed.

**Side effect:** the rotate ⟲/⟳ and height buttons no longer jump double in game 2. From game 2 on, the camera starts from the default angle instead of wherever game 1 left it.

BarkernotBob/blockchain.title: A second game in the same page load doubles every tap and the render loop [P0 bug]

BarkernotBob/blockchain.body:
Size: Quick
Source: UI/UX review 2026-09-22 (finding #1)

## Problem
Rotating a phone, resizing a desktop window, going fullscreen, or tablet split-view all leave the
3D board stuck at the size it first loaded. Reproduced 2026-09-22 in the built-in browser: started a
game at 375×812, widened to 1440×900 → canvas stayed 375×812, the rest of the screen was empty.

Root cause: `initThree()` calls `renderer.setSize(W, H)` (`app/main.js` ~4249). With its default
`updateStyle = true`, Three.js writes an inline pixel `width`/`height` onto `#gameCanvas`, overriding
the CSS `width:100%; height:100%`. The window `resize` handler (~4353) then measures
`cv.offsetWidth/offsetHeight` — i.e. the frozen inline size — so the size never changes.

Shared `main.js` → affects all four games.

## Fix direction
Pass `false` as the third argument (`renderer.setSize(W, H, false)`) in `initThree` and in the
resize handler, so CSS keeps controlling the display size and the renderer only sizes the drawing
buffer. Grep for any other `setSize(` calls.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Start a game at phone size, then widen to desktop: the board fills the whole window, undistorted.
- [ ] Shrink back to phone size: still fills, and the board stays in view (existing `computeFitRadius`
      pull-back still works).
- [ ] Canary in `variantTests` (every variant file — shared code): after init, `#gameCanvas` has no
      inline pixel width/height. Fails before the fix.
- [ ] `node app/build.mjs --all`; `node tests/run-tests.mjs --fast` green (run `--all` once since
      shared); `tests/baseline.json` bumped.
- [ ] Rendered in real Chrome at two sizes and screenshotted.

## Manual test (for Isaiah)
*(Written when the issue is completed — not before.)*

---

comments.body:
Plan: pass `false` as the third argument to both `renderer.setSize` calls in `app/main.js` (`initThree` and the window resize handler). CSS then keeps control of the canvas's display size, and Three.js only sizes the drawing buffer. Those are the only two `setSize` calls in the app. The resize handler also skips a 0x0 measurement (canvas hidden behind a menu), so the camera aspect can't become NaN.

Canary `canvas keeps no inline pixel size (init + resize)` goes in all four `variant.*.js` files (shared code). Checked with headless real Chrome (SwiftShader) at 375x812, then 1440x900, then 375x812, before and after the fix.

Fixed in #57 (merged).

**What changed:** the 3D view now follows the window. The canvas keeps its CSS size (full window) instead of freezing at whatever size it was when the game started. So widening the browser, rotating a phone, or going phone to desktop now re-fits the board.

**How it was verified:**
- New regression canary `canvas keeps no inline pixel size (init + resize)` in all four games. It failed before the fix and passes after.
- `node tests/run-tests.mjs --fast --all`: all green.
- Headless real Chrome: started a game at phone size, widened to desktop, then shrank back. The canvas measured 375x812, then 1440x900, then 375x812, and the board filled the window each time (screenshots in `docs/renders/1-resize-*.jpg`).

No manual test needed.
